stage_expectation_note: expected_on describes final symbolic-heap support, not phase1 alone. Phase1 retains old representation/capacity rejection thresholds while preserving allocation size expressions/snapshots. Phase2 enables symbolic byte-array storage; phase3 widens byte offsets only when the old signed domain is insufficient, with explicit serialization boundaries. Phase4 compact storage reuses symbolic slots' initial/runtime states and selects word cells only with a conservative CFG certificate.
scope: conversion/parser, structural checks, and planned fixed-input finite simulation; no model checking or C safety proofs
required_properties: Only source GOTO ASSERT roots; no heap-generated bad or path-pruning assume/constraint. Source assertions that query r_ok are intentional source properties.

cases.name: T1_original_nsqm_iff
cases.semantic_expectation: Supplied N=1 successful-allocation trace reaches the original source assertion failure (a[0]=2, required=1). A FALSE result alone cannot establish object isolation.
cases.note: Original source has no malloc failure guard. Do not replace its unsigned-int malloc parameter with size_t. Use the original file in place.

cases.name: T2_large_object_isolation
cases.semantic_expectation: On successful allocations a[0]=11 and b[8]=22 coexist, with distinct tags. Node/array counts must not grow with 4294967288 bytes.
cases.note: No OS allocation is run. The 32-bit model's two huge successful allocations use the existing abstract malloc success semantics; report this premise rather than a concrete 32-bit address-space allocation claim.

cases.name: T2_high_legal_offset
cases.semantic_expectation: Highest element's byte offset is 4294967280, never truncated to the existing low tag-offset payload. First and last bytes of two distinct objects remain isolated.
cases.note: Same abstract successful-allocation premise as T2. C sizeof(void*) and layout stay 4/8 bytes despite a wider hidden pointer encoding.

cases.name: T3_size_snapshot
cases.semantic_expectation: Actual supported __CPROVER_OBJECT_SIZE observations before/after n=1 both equal 24, and p[2]=7 is accessible.

cases.name: T2_symbolic_extent_small
cases.semantic_expectation: A non-singleton source size range 10..536870911 exercises symbolic byte-array storage. Supplied n=10 gives size 80 and last-element byte offset 72; a[0]=11, b[8]=22, last values 31/47 stay isolated. Target sizeof(void*) equals size_t.

cases.name: T2_symbolic_extent_large
cases.semantic_expectation: The same non-singleton size source, supplied n=536870911, gives two 4294967288-byte symbolic objects and last-element offset 4294967280. Tags and byte lanes remain isolated, with full target-width offset and unchanged C pointer sizeof. Different supplied traces do not establish C SAFE or standard-C equivalence.
cases.note: Use existing abstract successful-allocation semantics; do not infer real OS allocation feasibility.

cases.name: T4_same_object_alias
cases.semantic_expectation: Constant-capacity compatibility: q=p uses the same tag, offset and bytes; both observe 9.

cases.name: T5_last_legal
cases.semantic_expectation: Last 8-byte access at offset 16 is accessible; formed one-past at offset 24 preserves tag and is not r_ok for 8 bytes. No one-past dereference occurs.

cases.name: T5_one_past_ub
cases.semantic_expectation: Deliberate one-past dereference follows pre-existing backend totalization. Compare observed_one_past and observed_first_after_ub to a constant-size counterpart in the same backend; no C SAFE claim.

cases.name: T6_unbounded_event_count
cases.semantic_expectation: Constant-sized malloc in an unbounded nondet loop still rejects; one source site must not become one reusable identity.

cases.name: T6_three_events_one_site
cases.semantic_expectation: Three certified loop iterations use three distinct successful-allocation identities; constant capacity stays on the existing representation.

cases.name: T7_nondet_latch
cases.semantic_expectation: The n call executes once, both observations stay 3 and both size snapshots stay 24. Also replay with nondet input ports changing after their call frames to detect improper re-reading.

cases.name: T8_legal_mixed_bytes
cases.semantic_expectation: Little-endian union representation and legal unsigned-char alias expose the same 8/16/32/64-bit byte lanes. wide=0x112233445566AB88, short[0]=0xAB88, int[0]=0x5566AB88. No incompatible typed-pointer alias is used.

cases.name: T8_free_ub
cases.semantic_expectation: free flips r_ok from true to false and preserves tag/size. Deliberate post-free byte read/write follow existing live-independent totalization. Compare same-backend constant-size counterpart; no C SAFE claim.

cases.name: T8_symbolic_mixed_bytes
cases.semantic_expectation: A non-singleton n=2..536870911 range forces symbolic Array storage even in Mixed; at supplied n=3 the legal union/unsigned-char aliases expose consistent 8/16/32/64-bit lanes and size24. Compact word certification must fail and retain byte8 Array cells. The original singleton mixed-byte fixture separately preserves the old constant representation.

cases.name: T9_size_t_arithmetic
cases.semantic_expectation: sizeof(long long)*n evaluates in size_t: 8 bytes under ILP32, 4294967304 under LP64. object_size snapshots exactly that result.

cases.name: T8_symbolic_calloc_zero
cases.semantic_expectation: n ranges over 2..3 so capacity remains non-singleton. At supplied n=3, calloc produces one 24-byte zeroed object; untouched first/last words are zero even under a nonzero raw array seed. Writing p[0]=9 leaves the last word zero, and sizeof/pointer layout use target C semantics.

cases.name: T9_actual_malloc_parameter
cases.semantic_expectation: Original-style unsigned-int malloc receives 8 under its actual ILP32 target. Its LP64 declaration conflicts with the library size_t signature and is outside this fixture's target contract.

cases.name: T9_unsigned_function_parameter
cases.semantic_expectation: An unsigned-int wrapper receives 8 in both targets after the source function-parameter conversion, then calls standard size_t malloc with 8. Pre-call size_t product is 8 under ILP32 and 4294967304 under LP64.

cases.name: boundary_pointer_integer
cases.rejection_reason: wider hidden symbolic-heap pointer cannot be serialized to C uintptr_t faithfully
cases.semantic_expectation: Reject explicitly while wider hidden tags lack a C-width integer serialization; a hidden-width value must not be presented as sizeof(void*) or uintptr_t. Future support requires exact round-trip bytes/value semantics.

cases.name: boundary_addressable_pointer
cases.rejection_reason: wider hidden symbolic-heap pointer cannot be stored in C pointer-width object bytes faithfully
cases.semantic_expectation: Reject explicitly while addressable pointer object bytes cannot encode hidden tags. C pointer object layout stays 4/8 bytes. Future support requires exact pointer-store/load and byte-copy semantics.
